resources.string: Automatic status needs diagnostic access through a one-time ADB grant or optional Shizuku. Otherwise open Google diagnostics.
Google push server reachable (network probe only)
Probe failed; inspect the network or VPN. This does not prove GMS is disconnected.
Google Play services: installed and enabled
Google Play services: unavailable or disabled
Requests may be ignored. Confirm the result in diagnostics. Limited to once per minute.
Choose your apps to review push components, permissions and background settings.

Apps scanned: %1$d · FCM/GCM: %2$d · Chosen: %3$d\nAutostart — Enabled: %4$d · Disabled: %5$d · Partial: %6$d · Unknown: %7$d\nApps with detected issues appear first. Tap a row for checks and settings.
Choose the apps whose notifications matter to you.
No FCM/GCM components detected; another push channel may be used
A system-policy reference that other tools can also modify. Review the complete battery policy in Settings.
Notification permission granted; the master switch and channels still need review
Notification master switch and channels: review in Settings
Android battery-optimization exemption: %1$s (separate from HyperOS policy)
The app is marked stopped. Open it once and sign in before testing.
No stopped flag detected; this does not mean the process is running
Background process status is unavailable. Check recents locking manually; FCM normally does not require a resident app process.

Open the target app, return to recents, then use HyperOS’s lock action on its task card (often by long-pressing the card). Availability varies by launcher. Locking is optional and does not guarantee delivery.
Refresh on system-list and network changes
No persistent notification or scheduled wakeups. Checks pause when the process cannot run; use the tile to resume.
Off by default. Reads current GMS state. To keep checks available after stopping ADB-started Shizuku or turning off debugging, first grant app diagnostic access above.
The system setting is absent or cannot be read
The system returned an empty list
This settings or diagnostics page is unavailable on this device
Attempting a heartbeat request and network check. Verify the result in diagnostics.
Start Shizuku first, or leave the optional feature off

Lit with Connected means GMS was just observed connected. A grey disconnected icon with Disconnected means GMS was just observed disconnected. A question mark with Unknown means unreadable, not off. Use one-time ADB diagnostic access or optional Shizuku. Refreshes every 5 seconds while visible, with no polling when hidden. Tap to try a heartbeat and open diagnostics; this does not turn off GMS push.
Automatic refresh is partly unavailable. Return to this page or use Refresh to check again.
Access is available, but the system denied reading connection information. FCM state remains unknown.
This system does not support the connection query command.
The connection information format is not supported on this system.
Connection information timed out. Try checking again.
Connection information could not be read. Please retry.
Access is available, but the system returned no usable connection information.
Source: current GMS service state · %1$s. Refreshed only while the dashboard or quick-settings panel is visible, not continuous monitoring.
No readable GMS push service. Open Google diagnostics and retry; this does not prove disconnection.
The previous connection result expired. Waiting for a fresh read.
Could not refresh app checks. Please try again.
App diagnostic access: ready · Shizuku does not need to stay running
App diagnostic access: not granted or incomplete. Shizuku authorization is separate.
Read source: app diagnostic permissions · no running Shizuku required

Optional: connect this device to ADB and execute all three grant commands. Then return to the dashboard or expand the tile. The app reads the current GMS service using its own identity; Shizuku and wireless debugging can then be stopped.

These permissions allow system diagnostic and application usage reads. This app queries only current GMS connection information through this path; it does not write battery policies or the system list.

Grant:
%1$s

Revoke:
%2$s

Android normally retains these grants across app updates and reboot. Uninstalling, revoking access or OEM policy can remove them. Unreadable or unsupported state remains Unknown. This does not add continuous monitoring or guarantee notification delivery.
Could not open Shizuku. Make sure it is installed and start its service manually.
Complete Shizuku authorization and wait for its helper to connect, then tap this button again.

Use the connected Shizuku helper to grant DUMP and PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS to this app and allow usage access. These permissions can read system diagnostics and application usage information. This app uses them to read current GMS connection state.\n\nAfter successful verification, the app can check without a running Shizuku. You may then turn off Developer options and USB/wireless debugging. Android normally retains the grants; OEM policy, revocation or uninstalling can remove them.
App diagnostic access verified. Shizuku and debugging no longer need to stay on for these reads.
Diagnostic access is incomplete. Keep debugging enabled and retry after checking Shizuku. The system may restrict permission grants; manual ADB commands are available below.
